description: Capability-based privilege model (M6.5, option b). A process the kernel launches directly (`exec`, init) holds a privileged capability; a posix_spawn (SpawnArgs) child does not; libdunit SpawnProcess inherits it. The privileged musl_cap uses a read-only terminal diag, then its unprivileged posix_spawn child cap_child confirms a read-only diag is allowed, a mutating diag (mkfs.dunit) is EPERM, and killing a non-child (pid 1) is EPERM. Run: tools/qemu_test.py --build --markers-file tools/m6_cap_markers.json --post-boot-delay 3 --settle 4 --cmd-timeout 45 --timeout 220 --boot-timeout 120

required.claim: a privileged (console-launched) process may run a read-only terminal diagnostic
a read-only terminal diagnostic is allowed to an unprivileged process too
a mutating terminal diagnostic (mkfs.dunit) is denied to an unprivileged process with EPERM
an unprivileged process cannot kill a process that is not its child (EPERM)
the capability driver ran to completion with the kernel alive

forbidden.why: a privileged process could not run a read-only diagnostic
a read-only diagnostic was wrongly denied to an unprivileged process
an unprivileged process was allowed a mutating disk diagnostic
an unprivileged process was allowed to kill a non-child
could not spawn the unprivileged probe child
